amorphous carbamazepine (CBZ) and nicotinamid (NCT) form a cocrystal and that the crystallization kinetics of the cocrystal are different from those of the pure components and depend on the thermal history.

cocrystals can be generated by the melt-mediated transformation of amorphous equiatomic mixtures of carbamazepinetonicotinamide, and the kinetics of the melt-mediated transformation can be described by an Avrami-Erofeyev model.

amorphous solid dispersions of carbamazepinenicotinamide generate cocrystals by solid-state phase transformations and that the crystallization pathways and kinetics depend on the heating rate and thermal history.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cocrystallizations can occur from amorphous states and that thermal history can significantly influence the cocrystallizing phases.
cocrystallizations from the amorphs are possible, and that the cocrystallisation pathways and kinetics depend on the thermal history.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the cocrystallinity of amorphous mixtures is not only dependent on the molecular mobility of the amorphized mixture but also on the thermal history of the amorphization process and the subsequent heating rate.
the amorphization process can be used to generate cocrystals from a molecularly dispersed mixture of components.
the amorphization process can serve as a medium to induce cocrystallisation and to identify cocrystallising systems.
